title: Chanan HaNechba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Taanit 23b relates that he was the daughter’s son of Choni HaMe’agel and was very pious. When rain was needed, the Rabbis would send the schoolchildren to him; they would take hold of the hem of his cloak and say to him, “Father, father, give us rain.” He said before the Holy One, blessed be He: “Master of the world, do it for the sake of these, who cannot distinguish between the Father who gives rain and the father who does not give rain.” Why was he called Chanan HaNechba? Because he used to hide himself in the privy (he was very modest in the privy; and in Rabbeinu Chananel’s commentary: “We have a tradition that the sages sought to appoint him leader over the community, and he did not accept; he went and hid, therefore they called him Chanan HaNechba”). Seder HaDorot cites this from Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot, chapter 2, but Hyman does not find it in his received Jerusalem Talmud.

notes.text: The modesty interpretation and Rabbeinu Chananel’s leadership tradition remain distinct attributed explanations. Hyman’s reported absence from his Jerusalem Talmud is not a new exhaustive negative search.
